reason: The strainer is blocked, and the service tool may let me open or clear it. It is also the only offered action.
expectation: I expect to access or remove the sludge from the strainer, though restoring flow may take another step.

effect: Backflushing restored the water flow and left a residue sample to investigate, including some curled flecks.
reaction: I’m curious about the flecks and whether they differ from the fine material.
reason: The filter cloth may separate the residue into more useful fractions for examination; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the cloth to separate or collect some of the material, though I’m unsure which particles it will retain.

effect: The membrane separated the curled flecks, making their edge features easier to examine.
reaction: The regular projections make me curious about what the flecks are.
reason: The microscope is the only offered combination and should help investigate the particles blocking the intake.
expectation: I expect a closer view of the flecks, though I don't yet know what they are.

effect: The microscope revealed a segmented body with limbs in the strainer residue, and the record was sent to Earth. The chapter is complete, but what the body is remains uncertain.
reaction: I was surprised by the joints and limbs; the ordinary task of clearing a blockage suddenly became more intriguing.

mostWorthwhile.text: Examining the membrane under the microscope was most worthwhile: it turned the unusual flecks into a concrete observation and raised a compelling question about their origin.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filtering the residue was a useful preparation, but less engaging on its own than restoring flow or seeing the microscopic body.

surprise.text: The curled fleck resolved into a segmented body with limbs, rather than merely looking like an ordinary particle.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless: clearing the strainer, separating the flecks and examining them followed naturally from the goals. Each step had only one offered combination, though, so there was little decision-making.

continue.text: Yes. I would want to learn what Earth makes of the microscope record and where the body came from.
